Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) launched its holiday giving drive this morning. From November 2 to November 30, shoppers on Walmart.com and the Walmart app can round up their checkout totals for Operation Homefront, which supports military and veteran families. Walmart will match those donations 2:1, up to $1 million.

Sundry Photography / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

"Giving back is one of the greatest holiday traditions, and that's what A Season to Spark Good is all about," said Erin Hogue, Senior Director at Walmart.

This is the fourth consecutive year of the partnership. Walmart says the round-up program has raised more than $7.9 million for the nonprofit since 2023. Operation Homefront CEO Alan Reyes said, "We are deeply grateful for four years of continued support through Spark Good."

Refund Checks Tied to Walmart Money Counters Are Arriving Now

On October 15, the FTC announced it is mailing more than $9.8 million to consumers harmed by Walmart's alleged failure to stop scammers who took hundreds of millions of dollars from U.S. consumers through its wire transfer services. Walmart settled the charges in June 2025, agreeing to pay $10 million, Fox6 News reported. The FTC's case centers on whether Walmart properly warned customers, trained employees and secured its in-store transfer services against outside fraudsters.

title: Walmart doubles down on warehouse robots as holiday rush nears
detail:
Walmart doubles down on warehouse robots as holiday rush nears
Opeyemi Babalola, Celine Provini
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 10:33 AM MST 5 min read
WMT
SYM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

When I was young, I watched a lot of sci-fi movies, and robots were everywhere. They flew spaceships, fought wars, and even cleaned the house. I filed it all under someday.

It is 2026, and someday has apparently arrived early. It just did not start in our living rooms. It began in the warehouses behind our stores.

Walmart Inc. (WMT) made that plain on Thursday, Oct. 29. It expanded its deal with Symbotic Inc. (SYM), the Walmart-backed robot maker already working in its warehouses, according to a press release.

Walmart committed about $6 billion over several years. The work covers 25 U.S. regional distribution centers and other parts of its global network.

Symbotic has helped Walmart automate its supply chain since 2017, Reuters reported. Because the work spans years, this deal is less about this Christmas than the ones after it.

Also read: Walmart has a new plan to solve one of its customers' biggest problems

What Walmart is really buying with $6 billion

The $6 billion comes on top of existing contracts, according to a Symbotic SEC filing. One of those earlier deals already covers all 42 of Walmart's regional distribution centers.

Of that, $125 million funds research into next-generation racking and picking technology, the filing showed. Walmart is paying to shape the next machine, not just buying the current one.

The terms bind both sides tightly. Short of termination, the commitment cannot be cut unless both companies agree, and Walmart owes Symbotic money if it buys fewer systems than promised. The deal also restricts Symbotic from selling to one specified company, which the filing's summary leaves unnamed.

That last clause matters more than the dollar figure. It reads like a buyer protecting an edge. Walmart also owned about 13% of Symbotic as of September 2025, the annual report shows.

Symbotic is starting to look like Walmart's in-house robot maker.

On Thursday, October 29, 2026, Walmart committed about $6 billion over several years to expand its Symbotic warehouse automation deal.NurPhoto / Getty Images
Why the holiday rush makes this deal matter

Walmart is stretching its holiday sales this year. Its three deal events run from Thursday, Nov. 12, through Wednesday, Dec. 2. The events add up to 14 days of deals, up from 10 in 2025, Retail Dive reported.

More sale days mean more trucks to fill and more online orders to pull from storage. E-commerce made up about 23% of Walmart U.S. sales in the quarter ended July 31, 2026, according to its earnings summary. The warehouse now serves the doorstep as much as the aisle.

Walmart said the systems should bring wider selection, faster service, and steadier restocking. Rob Montgomery, a Walmart executive vice president, said the work helps it "improve service, grow capacity, simplify work for our associates and lower costs."

title: Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections

Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections

Trading disclosure

Even Nvidia doesn't want its shares on OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

The chipmaker is among 12 new companies listed as objecting issuers in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Friday. The others are Costco, Nike, Micron, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Reddit, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Corning, Bloom Energy, IREN, and USA Rare Earth. The additions bring the total to 50 companies.

It's the largest single batch yet. The list stood at 38 in the venue's Oct. 28 notice, when Walmart and Eli Lilly joined, and at nine when the first objectors appeared on Oct. 15. It has more than quintupled since.

The newcomers span chips, cybersecurity, retail, and energy. Nvidia, Micron, and Corning join hardware peers such as AMD, Intel, and Broadcom, while CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks bring cybersecurity heavyweights to the list. IREN, a Bitcoin miner that has expanded into AI cloud computing, adds a name from the crypto industry itself.

Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. The objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks around the clock. Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

None of the objecting companies have explained their decisions, but Nasdaq offered one possible rationale when it opted its own shares out of the exemption.

A spokesperson told The Wall Street Journal that Nasdaq doesn't want its stock trading on a venue that doesn't show the best prices in real time or report trades to the consolidated tape.

Further, Crypto in America reported that Nasdaq may be playing a role behind the scenes in encouraging companies to opt out of the OKX-ICE venture. "Our Nasdaq rep had reached out to us regarding OKX listing, suggesting we should object and that they would hold a call to discuss why," an executive at a Nasdaq-listed company told the publication. "Nasdaq is definitely partly behind this," the exec reportedly said.

Walmart Blocks Its Stock From OKX-ICE Tokenized Trading Venue

OKXICE's notice acknowledges it isn't subject to Regulation NMS, the rules designed to ensure investors get the best displayed prices. It also warns that broker-dealers face unsettled questions about trade reporting and best execution on the venue.

Some of the market's biggest names, including Apple, Tesla and Amazon, still haven't appeared on the list.

Why Walmart (WMT) is Poised to Beat Earnings Estimates Again

If you are looking for a stock that has a solid history of beating earnings estimates and is in a good position to maintain the trend in its next quarterly report, you should consider Walmart (WMT). This company, which is in the Zacks Retail - Supermarkets industry, shows potential for another earnings beat.

This world's largest retailer has seen a nice streak of beating earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The average surprise for the last two quarters was 6.25%.

For the last reported quarter, Walmart came out with earnings of $0.81 per share versus the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.73 per share, representing a surprise of 10.96%. For the previous quarter, the company was expected to post earnings of $0.65 per share and it actually produced earnings of $0.66 per share, delivering a surprise of 1.54%.

Price and EPS Surprise

Thanks in part to this history, there has been a favorable change in earnings estimates for Walmart lately. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the stock is positive, which is a great indicator of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Walmart currently has an Earnings ESP of +1.35%, which suggests that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This positive Earnings ESP when combined with the stock's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) indicates that another beat is possibly around the corner. We expect the company's next earnings report to be released on November 19, 2026.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Wayfair Inc. W is slated to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4.

For the third quarter of 2026, Wayfair expects revenues to grow at a high-single-digit rate year over year. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for W's third-quarter revenues is pegged at $3.36 billion, indicating 7.84% year-over-year growth.

The consensus mark for earnings is pegged at 82 cents per share, which has remained unchanged over the past 30 days, suggesting an improvement of 17.14% from the year-ago quarter.

Wayfair surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings in three of the trailing four quarters and met once, delivering an average surprise of 21.51%. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered an earnings surprise of 1.06%.

Let us see how things have shaped up for the upcoming announcement.

Factors Shaping Wayfair's Q3 Results

Wayfair's continued market share gains and strengthening order trends are likely to have supported revenue growth in the third quarter of 2026. In the preceding quarter, U.S. revenues increased 8.7% year over year, while orders delivered grew 6% to 10.6 million and active customers increased 3.3% to 21.7 million. New-order growth also accelerated for the fourth consecutive quarter, reflecting improving customer acquisition. Supported by competitive pricing, broader product selection and faster delivery capabilities, these favorable trends are expected to have boosted Wayfair's revenues in the quarter under review.

Wayfair's expanding customer loyalty initiatives and omnichannel presence are expected to have strengthened customer engagement and repeat purchases in the to-be-reported quarter. Programs such as Wayfair Rewards, Wayfair Verified and Wayfair Delivery Plus continue to enhance product discovery, value and delivery convenience. Repeat buyers accounted for 80.2% of total orders in the second quarter. Meanwhile, recently opened Wayfair stores in Atlanta and Columbus expanded customer acquisition opportunities, with more than half of store customers being new to the company's customer base. These initiatives likely supported higher order volumes and sustained market share gains in the third quarter.

Strength across Wayfair's specialty retail brands and luxury platform, Perigold, is likely to have provided additional growth opportunities in the third quarter. Specialty brands recorded nearly 20% year-over-year growth in the second quarter, while Perigold grew more than 35%. Perigold's active customer base approached 400,000, increasing nearly 20% year over year, with customers spending almost three times as much annually as typical Wayfair shoppers. The platform's expanding product assortment, growing trade business and white-glove delivery services, supported by Wayfair's logistics and technology infrastructure, are expected to have strengthened higher-value order growth in the quarter under review.

However, subdued housing activity and an uneven consumer recovery are likely to have constrained Wayfair's growth in the third quarter. Although the U.S. home goods category showed signs of stabilization in the second quarter, housing turnover remained depressed, with improvements concentrated among higher-income consumers. Persistent inflation, elevated interest rates and a highly promotional retail environment may have restricted discretionary spending on furniture and home furnishings. These challenging conditions are anticipated to have affected customer purchasing decisions, potentially limiting order growth and revenue momentum in the to-be-reported quarter.

Wayfair's international business is also likely to have faced continued demand-related challenges in the third quarter. International revenues declined 1.3% year over year in the second quarter, or 2% on a constant-currency basis, reflecting subdued consumer sentiment and discretionary spending in Canada and the United Kingdom. The comparatively delayed rollout of customer engagement initiatives, including loyalty programs, across certain international markets may also have limited near-term growth opportunities. These factors are expected to have constrained international revenues and partially offset the company's strong domestic performance in the quarter under review.
